subject: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, May 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing

Team — sharing the first pass of the finserv target list for the regulated workloads ABM pilot.

Asks (by EOD Monday if possible, but any feedback today helps):
1) Additions/removals: what should we *definitely* include or exclude for v1?
2) Prioritization logic: does the scoring match what Sales is seeing (intent + fit + ability to run a 2–4 week pilot)?
3) Routing: please mark NA vs EMEA coverage and suggested AE owner (Stephanie/Lukas — would love your input).

Notes on filters used:
- Regulated/controlled environments (audit + retention requirements; preference for VPC/private)
- Strong platform/ML or security involvement (CISO/IT Security + Platform Eng)
- Workloads where Dedicated/Private is a clean fit (fraud ops, call center summarization, risk/compliance, advisor tools)

Links:
- Working sheet (comments enabled): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FinservTargetAccountsV1
- Exported attachment for offline review

Attachment stubs:
- Finserv_Target_Accounts_v1.xlsx (export)
- Scoring_Rubric_v1.pdf

Flag anything that looks off from a compliance-claims perspective too.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Growth Marketing (ABM)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, May 3, 2025 at 10:06 AM
Subject: Re: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing

Ben — this is a solid start. A few quick notes from NA coverage:

Adds (NA):
- Northbridge Banking (already warming; security team engaged; strong VPC requirement)
- Orion Payments (payments/fraud ops + support; they care about latency + audit)
- Brightline Insurance (compliance heavy; questionnaire style org)
- Regal Wealth Management (wealth/advisor workflows; strict SSO + audit logging)

Removes / deprioritize:
- Any accounts where the obvious first use case is “marketing copy / generic chatbot” with no security buyer. Those won’t convert to Private/Dedicated.
- A couple of the very small credit unions on the list (unless we have an intro) — they’ll eat cycles with procurement without budget for Dedicated.

Routing suggestion (NA):
- Avery: Orion Payments + 3–4 similar mid-enterprise fintech/payment processors
- Priyom: Brightline + insurance cluster
- Diego: the “fast-moving fintech” cluster (if any are truly security-driven)

On scoring: I’d weight “evidence of security process” higher (mentions of SOC2, SAML/SCIM, retention, audit logs). Those are the ones where our talk track lands.

Happy to do a 20 min working session to finalize routing.

— Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
NA Sales Leader
Redwood Inference

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, May 3, 2025 at 11:22 AM
Subject: Re: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing

+1 to Steph’s point on weighting “security process present.”

EMEA thoughts:

Adds (EMEA):
- 2–3 mid/large retail banks where we can lean on data residency + private networking requirements (even if we start with Dedicated in-region, they’ll ask about Private).
- One payments processor in DACH or Nordics that’s already investing in fraud tooling (often a clear pilot: rerank + summarize + case notes).

Removes / caution:
- Anything headquartered in EU with strict “no US processors” policies unless we *know* we can meet the topology requirement. It’s a fast ‘no’ otherwise.

Routing (EMEA):
- Hannah should own the strict-compliance accounts (SSO/SAML required, audit export requirements).
- I can take 3–5 exec-touch accounts personally if we think they’re good lighthouse candidates.

One request: can we add a column for “data residency / region requirement (known/unknown)” and “deployment preference (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)”? It will reduce back-and-forth once outreach starts.

Lukas
Lukas Meyer
EMEA Sales Leader
Redwood Inference

From: Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, May 3, 2025 at 12:04 PM
Subject: Re: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing

I did a quick hygiene pass on the export:

- Found duplicates/near-duplicates (same parent company w/ different subsidiary names). If we’re routing to NA/EMEA, we should normalize to the parent and then list sub-entities as “business units” where relevant.
- Recommend we separate “intent signals” into two fields:
  1) Redwood intent (site visits, benchmark download, docs/pricing page hits)
  2) Market intent (job postings, vendor comparisons, partner co-sell signals)

Scoring suggestion (simple + explainable):
- Fit (regulated + deployment constraints) = 0–5
- Security buying signals = 0–5
- Technical readiness (platform team exists, pilot-friendly) = 0–5
- Timing/budget indicators = 0–5

Also: if we’re going to use HubSpot lists, let’s lock the account naming conventions now (or the dashboard will be messy).

If you want, I can create the initial HubSpot list + properties once we agree on the columns.

Isabelle
Isabelle Laurent
CRM Hygiene & Pipeline Analytics
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, May 3, 2025 at 1:37 PM
Subject: Re: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing

From messaging/positioning POV, I’d add one more “qualifying” field in the sheet:

- Primary persona entry point (Security/CISO vs Platform Eng vs Product/Operations)

Reason: the first-touch copy and CTA should differ:
- Security-led: offer “security review / evidence pack intro” CTA
- Platform-led: offer “benchmark + architecture review” CTA

Also a caution on claims: for regulated accounts, we should avoid language implying specific certifications/coverage beyond what’s in the approved FAQ. The list itself is internal, but how we segment will influence outreach templates.

I’ll add a note in the sheet comments with recommended segment labels:
- “Audit + retention heavy”
- “Data residency sensitive”
- “SSO/SAML gate”
- “Pilot likely (2–4 weeks)”

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, May 3, 2025 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: Finserv target account list v1 — review + NA/EMEA routing

This is great — thank you.

Actioning updates now:
- Adding columns: data residency requirement (known/unknown), deployment preference (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), primary persona entry point
- Updating scoring to weight “security process present” (questionnaire, SSO/SAML, retention/audit asks)
- Normalizing parent/subsidiary naming (Isabelle — yes, please proceed on HubSpot properties after I update the sheet)

Proposed NA/EMEA routing approach (v1):
- NA: Stephanie to finalize AE mapping (Avery/Priyom/Diego) for the top 20; I’ll tag “pilot likely” cluster for SE bandwidth planning.
- EMEA: Lukas/Hannah to own strict-compliance accounts; I’ll split out a separate tab for “EU residency sensitive / Private-first” so we don’t accidentally run Hosted-led outreach.

I also added Steph’s priority accounts (Northbridge, Orion, Brightline, Regal) into the Tier 1 group.

Next step:
- I’ll send an updated v1 list Monday AM with Tier 1/2 locked and owner assignments.
- Grace: once owners are set, let’s align on sequence timing + handoff rules (who sends touch 1 vs touch 2).

Sheet is still the source of truth: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FinservTargetAccountsV1

Ben
Ben Carter
Growth Marketing (ABM)
Redwood Inference
